Track record

How the forecasts have scored

Two kinds of evidence, kept apart. Test results: how each published model scored on years held back from its development, in tests written down before the data was scored. Live record: how the forecasts we actually published scored once their windows closed. If a live model is not scored yet, this page says so directly. It also shows any scoring backlogs.

Live record, by model version

Every model version that has published a number, including retired ones. A score is shown only once 10 or more events have been observed for that version: with fewer, a model that always says “no” would look as good as a skilful one.

Does a 10% forecast come true 1 time in 10?

Calibration compares what was forecast with what happened. The published tornado model’s 2025 test, split by how high the forecast was. Live calibration is measured once enough forecasts with events have closed.
